# 1. Parts and tools

Prices are rough, to give an idea. Shop around. A cheap resistor kit and a box of pin
headers cover most of the small parts.

> [!NOTE]
> 📷 **Photo to add:** all the parts laid out on a table, before building.

## Electronics

| ✓ | Part | How many | About | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ☐ | Raspberry Pi 3 B+ | 1 | €40 | A Pi 4 also works |
| ☐ | Raspberry Pi HQ Camera (IMX477) | 1 | €55 | Used without its lens. You do not need to buy a lens |
| ☐ | Camera ribbon cable | 1 | | Comes with the camera |
| ☐ | 28BYJ-48 5 V stepper motor + ULN2003 driver board | 1 | €4 | Sold together |
| ☐ | 5 V fan, 30 × 30 mm | 1 | €5 | A Pi case fan. Measure it: some are 25 mm |
| ☐ | NeoPixel string (WS2811 or WS2812, 5 V) | 1 | €8 | Sold as "Christmas lights". Only one pixel is used |
| ☐ | Proto HAT for the Pi ("RPi Proto HAT w/EEP") | 1 | €5 | Must have strips like [the drawing](hat.md) |
| ☐ | 2 × 20 female header (socket) | 1 | €1 | Often comes with the HAT |
| ☐ | Male pin headers (a strip you can break) | 11 pins | €1 | 4 + 2 + 3 + 2 |
| ☐ | IRLZ44N MOSFET (TO-220, 3 legs) | 1 | €1 | Not an AO3400 (too small for the holes), not the blue IRF520 boards |
| ☐ | Resistor 220 Ω (red red brown) | 1 | | |
| ☐ | Resistor 100 kΩ (brown black yellow) | 1 | | |
| ☐ | Resistor 330 Ω (orange orange brown) | 1 | | 220 to 470 Ω also works |
| ☐ | Diode 1N5819 or 1N4148 | 1 | | |
| ☐ | Insulated wire, thin | ~30 cm | | 2 colours helps (red and black) |
| ☐ | Female jumper wires (Dupont) | ~10 | €2 | To connect the driver board, if your parts don't have plugs |
| ☐ | 5.1 V 2.5 A micro USB power supply | 1 | €10 | Use a proper one. Weak supplies make the Pi crash |
| ☐ | microSD card, 32 GB or more | 1 | €10 | Pictures are big |

## Other parts

| ✓ | Part | How many | About | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ☐ | Clear tape, 19 mm wide | 1 roll | €3 | "Crystal clear", not frosted. The roll's core must be about 26 mm inside |
| ☐ | PLA or PETG filament | ~200 g | €5 | PLA is fine indoors. Use PETG outside. The LED tower should be **black** |
| ☐ | Kitchen foil and a fine needle | | | Optional, for a smaller pinhole |

## Tools

- 3D printer
- Soldering iron and solder
- Fume extractor or a fan blowing the smoke away, and an open window
- Side cutters and a wire stripper
- Multimeter with a beep (continuity) mode
- Electrical tape or masking tape (holds parts while you solder)
- Small screwdriver set (for the camera)
- A blower (a camera lens blower) to get dust off the sensor
- Laptop with an SD card reader
- A ruler or calipers

## Measure before you print

The 3D model has a few sizes you should check against your own parts. They are listed in
[Print the parts](print.md#check-your-sizes-first). Have the tape roll, fan and camera at hand.
